why: Both files' docstrings describe real, previously-shipped user-visible bugs (TS-10: Back+Forward through the wizard silently discarded the user's deadline choice; TS-2: the goal step showed the full-curriculum item count instead of the wizard-selected scope). Neither test ever calls tester.pumpWidget — they only construct the widget object and assert the constructor stored the field verbatim, which Dart's own field assignment guarantees trivially. A future refactor that keeps the field but breaks the `initState`/`build` logic that actually consumes it (step_goal.dart:76-88 for TS-10, :351-359 for TS-2) would leave both tests green while silently reintroducing the exact bugs they claim to guard. Confirmed via repo-wide grep: no other test file in the tree pumps SelfPacedGoalStep with a non-null initialGoal or scopeSelections and asserts on the rendered/emitted result.
recommendation: Rewrite both as widget tests: for TS-10, pump SelfPacedGoalStep with initialGoal set to a deadline-type GoalEntity and assert the deadline card renders active (not blurred) and/or that tapping Continue immediately emits goalType=='deadline' with the restored targetDate. For TS-2, pump with non-empty scopeSelections and content items outside the selection, and assert the rendered item-count/estimate reflects only the selected scope, not the full set.
acceptance_criteria: goal_step_ts10_state_preserve_test.dart pumps the widget with a deadline initialGoal and asserts observable deadline-mode state (not just constructor storage) — fails if initState stops reading widget.initialGoal

self_paced_goal_step_scope_test.dart pumps the widget with scopeSelections + a mixed content fixture and asserts the rendered/emitted count is scoped, not the full-curriculum total — fails if the scoping logic regresses
